content:
Academics # 🎯 Academic Focus & Future Goals # My academic interests form a multi-disciplinary arc — starting from the core of Electrical and Computer Engineering (EE/ECE) and extending toward Business, Applied Mathematics, and Quantitative Finance.
At heart, I’m driven by the idea of building systems that connect precision, computation, and real-world utility:
In EE/ECE, I’m fascinated by embedded systems, sensor design, and human–machine interfaces — how hardware and data can empower decision-making. In Business & Applied Math, I enjoy modeling uncertainty and optimizing limited resources, whether in markets or in engineering design. In Quantitative Finance, I find beauty in using stochastic models and data to forecast complex systems — merging mathematical intuition with strategic insight. In Physics, I see the foundation of everything: understanding the rules before designing around them. This blend of disciplines allows me to think like an engineer, reason like a scientist, and act like a builder.
📚 AP Coursework & Academic Rigor # I pursue one of the most rigorous course loads at Wyoming Seminary, combining both STEM and humanities to strengthen analytical and expressive thinking.
AP Courses Completed or in Progress:
STEM: Physics C (Mechanics & E&M), Calculus BC, Chemistry, Statistics, Computer Science Principles Social Sciences & Humanities: Macroeconomics, European History, English Language & Composition, English Literature Independent Studies: Advanced Electronics, Quantitative Research Projects, and Data Modeling Each course gives me tools to bridge technical and human perspectives — from vector calculus in electromagnetism to data interpretation in economics.
🧠 Academic Awards & Research Recognition # PJAS (Pennsylvania Junior Academy of Science) — Two-time Award Winner, recognized for original research in optical sensing and material systems, including a Surface Plasmon Resonance–based bacterial detection prototype. HIMCM (High School Mathematical Modeling Contest) — First Prize, for developing a statistical model integrating environmental and behavioral variables. Science Olympiad — Medaled in Electric Vehicle and Robot Tour events for applying mechanical design and coding principles. Dean’s High Honor Roll — Recognized for consistent excellence across advanced STEM and humanities coursework. Beyond competitions, I continuously challenge myself with open-source projects, exploring circuit design, algorithm optimization, and AI-assisted prototyping through GitHub and online engineering communities.
💡 Intellectual Philosophy # To me, academics isn’t about collecting scores — it’s about building frameworks for understanding.
Engineering teaches how things work; business teaches why decisions matter; and mathematics teaches how to measure uncertainty.
When these three intersect, they create something powerful: clarity amidst complexity.
That’s the mindset I carry into every experiment, every class, and every project I design.
summary: Where engineering curiosity meets data-driven thinking.

content:
🌱 Roots & Family # I was born on July 31, 2006 in Hong Kong. I’m the eldest of three: a sister born in 2008 and a brother born in 2011. 👦👧👦
My father leads in a Buddhist Association 🧘‍♂️, and my mother was a lawyer ⚖️ who found her own law office.
My earliest moral compass came from my grand-uncle—affectionately “Grandpa Buddha.” 🙏
He devoted his life to sharing compassion through education and media, showing me that kindness can scale when paired with technology and discipline. His calm presence taught me to look for solutions that help people, not just impress them. 💡💻
🎒 Early Education # Kindergarten: I started in Shenzhen and then transferred to Hong Kong, spending four years there. 🧸 Primary School: Attended the Hong Kong Alliance Primary School (public) through Grade 5. 🏫 Grade 5–6: Transferred to BASIS International School Park Lane Harbor. 🌏 I planned to attend middle school in the U.S. to pursue my hockey dream, and I even visited schools in person. 🏒
Then COVID-19 arrived. and I had been transferred between 3 schools within 3 years. 🔄
🏫 Finding My Path at Wyoming Seminary # Sem became the place where I rebuilt from the ground up. Through consistent effort and self-direction, I learned to be independent, organized, and resilient. 💪
Along the way, I grew into roles that I once thought were out of reach:
Student Government President 🗳️ Club leadership in engineering and international communities 🤝 Varsity athletics across hockey, golf, and tennis 🏒⛳🎾 Campus service and student-led initiatives 🌟 Sem changed me more than I expected. I’m grateful for the trust the school placed in me and I see it as a gift I must grow and pass on. 🎁
💭 What This Journey Means to Me # Frequent moves taught me to adapt, listen, and lead without losing empathy. The pandemic taught me to start over—sometimes more than once. 🔁
My family and “Grandpa Buddha” taught me that compassion is not passive; it is a daily practice that should inform how we design systems, study, compete, and collaborate. ❤️
I carry that forward now: to build with kindness, to serve my community, and to turn opportunity into shared progress. 🚀
summary: From Hong Kong to Pennsylvania — a journey of resilience and purpose.

content:
I’m a student, engineer, and athlete exploring here at Wyoming Seminary School who wanted to know how technology and business generate positive real-world impact.
⚙️ Engineering Exploration # I’ve spent years building and experimenting with projects that bridge science and usability — from a transparent OLED hockey display that displays tactical cues during games, to a Surface Plasmon Resonance (SPR) biosensor detecting bacterial data.
🤝 Community Impact # Outside the classroom, I founded SponsorX, an athletic sponsorship platform, and Free Youth Hockey Camp endorsed by Shenzhen Ice Hockey Association to promote local hockey development
🏒 Athletics # Sports have been everywhere part of my life.
Ice Hockey — Four years of Prep Team Player, competing in MPHL and NEPSAC. Golf — Three-year Varsity player, having a steady of 75-85 shot. Tennis — Three-year Varsity player, 2025 PIAA District 2 Team and Double Champion.
I’ve also enjoyed playing baseball and volleyball, learning how rhythm, focus, and teamwork carry across every sport. Athletics taught me discipline and composure — lessons that fuel my resilience in engineering and leadership alike.
# 🌟 Everyday Life # Beyond projects and sports, I’m someone who loves to make people laugh and create warmth in every room I walk into.
I’m the kind of friend who listens, helps others through tough times, and turns stress into motivation.
I had given exploration of everything I interested and loved with during high school to find the path I want to take in future. For now, I think my dream lays between Techno-Business, where merges my skill of Electrical Engineering with Business insight.
